S001.name: Detail_Inattention_Errors
S001.description: Often fails to give close attention to details or makes careless mistakes.
examples: Makes mistakes in homework or tests by misreading questions or skipping important parts.
Frequently omits details or makes typos in work documents or reports.
Repeats mistakes in calculations or numerical work, such as switching signs or getting digits wrong.
Performs tasks incorrectly by missing important details in instructions.

S004.name: Instruction_Follow through_Difficulty
S004.description: Often does not follow through on instructions and fails to finish schoolwork, chores, or duties in the workplace.
examples: Starts homework or projects but fails to complete them, submitting unfinished work or missing deadlines.
When given multi-step instructions, follows only the first few steps and forgets the rest.
Starts cleaning or organizing but switches to another task midway, failing to finish.
Leaves almost completed work reports or paperwork unfinished, neglecting the final steps.

S007.name: Losing_Items
S007.description: Often loses things necessary for tasks or activities.
examples: Frequently loses school supplies or office supplies like pens, erasers, and calculators.
Always searching for glasses, cell phones, wallets, or keys because they do not know where they are.
Loses necessary documents or materials at home or in the office and cannot find them.
Cannot remember where they placed an item they were holding just moments ago.

S008.name: Distractibility
S008.description: Often easily distracted by extraneous stimuli (for older adolescents and adults, may include unrelated thoughts).
examples: Easily distracted and stops working due to small noises or movements nearby.
Cannot concentrate because eyes keep wandering to the scenery outside the window or people passing by.
Starts daydreaming or gets sidetracked by sudden thoughts while working or studying.
Loses focus and listens in when hearing side conversations or TV sounds.

S009.name: Daily_Activities_Forgetfulness
S009.description: Often forgetful in daily activities (e.g., doing chores, running errands; for older adolescents and adults, returning calls, paying bills, keeping appointments).
examples: Forgets appointment times or meeting schedules, arriving late or missing them entirely.
Forgets to reply to received calls or messages for days.
Frequently incurs late fees because of missing deadlines for utility bills or credit card payments.
Forgets to take medication or leaves necessary items at home when going out.

S012.name: Feeling_Restless
S012.description: Often runs about or climbs in situations where it is inappropriate. (Note: In adolescents or adults, may be limited to feeling restless.)
examples: Feels uncomfortable and restless as if something is squirming inside when sitting still.
Feels internally anxious and stifled in situations requiring prolonged sitting.
A sense of urgency and anxiety that one must keep moving or doing something.
Feels unable to endure staying still and must constantly be doing something.

S013.name: Quiet_Activity_Difficulty
S013.description: Often unable to play or engage in leisure activities quietly.
examples: Unable to engage in calm activities for long, such as reading quietly or drawing.
Cannot play quietly, often shouting or making loud noises during games or play.
Unable to stay quiet in quiet places like libraries or movie theaters, making noise.
Cannot endure and avoids quiet and calm activities like meditation or yoga.

S014.name: Constant_Activity
S014.description: Is often 'on the go', acting as if 'driven by a motor'.
examples: Constantly moving and active as if driven by a motor.
Starts another task immediately after finishing one, without resting for a moment.
Unable to stay still even on weekends or days off, constantly doing something.
Appears to others to be always busy and bustling about.

S016.name: Blurting_Answers
S016.description: Often blurts out an answer before a question has been completed.
examples: Raises hand or blurts out the answer before the question is even finished in class or meetings.
Jumps to conclusions and speaks before the other person finishes their sentence.
Answers hastily without reading the question to the end in quizzes or exams.
Interrupts and answers in the middle of a conversation without listening to the other person until the end.

S017.name: Waiting_Turn_Difficulty
S017.description: Often has difficulty waiting his or her turn.
examples: Cannot wait and cuts in line or gets impatient when standing in a queue.
Rushes or cuts in without waiting for their turn in games or board games.
Keeps checking the time or complaining when waiting for their turn at hospitals or public offices.
Fidgets, complains, or gets annoyed in situations where waiting for a turn is required.

symptom.disease_info: Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD), Combined Presentation, is characterized by a persistent pattern of both inattentive and hyperactive-impulsive behaviors that are inconsistent with developmental level and cause impairment in multiple settings. It typically begins in childhood, though many adults present later when environmental demands exceed their coping strategies or when long-standing traits begin to interfere more clearly with work, relationships, or health management. Core features include difficulties with sustained attention, organization, and follow-through, as well as restlessness, impulsive decision-making, and acting without adequate forethought, and these must be present for at least 6 months and traceable back to earlier development. Clinically, it is distinguished from anxiety, mood disorders, and normal distractibility by its early onset, cross-situational pervasiveness, and enduring pattern of executive function difficulties rather than symptoms occurring only during discrete episodes or specific stressors.

patient.personality: Alver is a quiet, introspective tech enthusiast who is methodical when engaged with his interests and enjoys solitary, creative and meditative activities.
patient.stressor: Alver transitioned from high school to his first full-time job in technical support about a year ago, moving from self-paced schoolwork and independent hobbies to a help-desk environment with constant tickets, chat messages, and background office activity. Initially excited, he tried to absorb everything at once—learning new systems, scripting, and documenting solutions—while also keeping up with his creative projects and online interests during breaks. Over time, he found that the open-plan office, frequent notifications, and rapidly shifting priorities made it increasingly hard for him to stay with a single task, and unresolved tickets began to accumulate as he bounced between interruptions and his own wandering thoughts. After several performance reviews noting incomplete work and the need for closer supervision, and feeling frustrated that his intelligence and effort weren’t translating into consistent output, he sought psychiatric help to understand why he was having so much trouble keeping his focus in this new environment.
patient.chief_complaint: “At work I can’t seem to stay focused on one thing—every little noise, message, or random thought pulls me away from what I’m supposed to be doing.”

S001.name: Detail_Inattention_Errors
S001.description: Often fails to give close attention to details or makes careless mistakes.
S001.manifestation: With the tickets, I’ll think I’ve read everything, but then my lead points out I missed a line in the description or typed the wrong IP address, and it’s always some tiny detail I somehow skim right past even when I’m trying to be careful.

S004.name: Instruction_Follow through_Difficulty
S004.description: Often does not follow through on instructions and fails to finish schoolwork, chores, or duties in the workplace.
S004.manifestation: I’ll start working on a support ticket or a documentation page, get about three-quarters done, then something pings me or a coworker asks a question, and I never quite get back to finishing the original thing unless someone reminds me.

S007.name: Losing_Items
S007.description: Often loses things necessary for tasks or activities.
S007.manifestation: At least a couple times a week I’m wandering around the office or my apartment looking for my badge, my earbuds, or the little notebook I use for scripts, even though I swear I just had it in my hand a minute ago.

S008.name: Distractibility
S008.description: Often easily distracted by extraneous stimuli (for older adolescents and adults, may include unrelated thoughts).
S008.manifestation: When I’m on a call or typing up notes, my mind will suddenly drift to a random idea for a script, a game I’m playing, or a conversation happening two desks over, and before I realize it I’ve lost the thread of what I was doing.

S009.name: Daily_Activities_Forgetfulness
S009.description: Often forgetful in daily activities (e.g., doing chores, running errands; for older adolescents and adults, returning calls, paying bills, keeping appointments).
S009.manifestation: I keep meaning to call people back, pay a bill, or reply to a message from my supervisor, and then I’ll notice days later that it’s still sitting there unread or flagged because I just spaced out on it once it left my immediate screen.

S012.name: Feeling_Restless
S012.description: Often runs about or climbs in situations where it is inappropriate. (Note: In adolescents or adults, may be limited to feeling restless.)
S012.manifestation: Sitting through long team meetings or even just waiting on hold with a user, I feel this restless buzz in my body like I need to move or do something else, and I’ll catch myself bouncing my leg or shifting around a lot without even noticing.

S013.name: Quiet_Activity_Difficulty
S013.description: Often unable to play or engage in leisure activities quietly.
S013.manifestation: Even with stuff I enjoy, like trying to meditate or reading tech blogs, I find myself fidgeting, checking my phone, or putting on background noise because just doing one quiet thing without any extra stimulation starts to feel uncomfortable after a few minutes.

S014.name: Constant_Activity
S014.description: Is often 'on the go', acting as if 'driven by a motor'.
S014.manifestation: My coworkers joke that I never really sit still because I’m always swiveling in my chair, getting up to refill my water, checking another screen, or starting some side project the moment there’s the slightest lull.

S016.name: Blurting_Answers
S016.description: Often blurts out an answer before a question has been completed.
S016.manifestation: In stand-up meetings, I’ll jump in with a solution or an answer to a question before my manager has finished explaining the problem, and sometimes it turns out I’ve missed an important part of what they were actually asking.

S017.name: Waiting_Turn_Difficulty
S017.description: Often has difficulty waiting his or her turn.
S017.manifestation: I get noticeably impatient in queues or when I’m waiting for my turn to speak in group chats or games, and I’ll keep checking the time or almost cut people off because it feels weirdly hard to just sit there and wait.
